Fine-grained layer-wise pruning, when applied without fine-tuning, yields larger accuracy drops than global unstructured pruning.
(on Cora node classification, accuracy drops from 0.86 at baseline to 0.76 at 90% sparsity without fine-tuning),

(accuracy recovers to approximately 0.89 at 90% sparsity after fine-tuning).
On tasks other than structurally sensitive tasks, fine-grained pruning with fine-tuning does not recover baseline accuracy at high sparsity.

For the datasets in Table 5, the model size ratio grows with sparsity under both pruning approaches.

For Cora node classification and link prediction in Table 5, the model size ratios from fine-grained and global pruning were nearly identical, implying that the specifics of pruning matter little for this dataset.
For BBBP in Table 5, fine-grained pruning yields larger size ratios (base size / pruned size) than global pruning—5.79 versus 4.49 at 80% sparsity, and 8.71 versus 7.72 at 90% sparsity.
In Table 5's Proteins dataset, the model size ratio for global pruning fell from 3.13 to 1.9 as sparsity rose, while fine-grained pruning stayed stable and reached a peak of 8.32.
Based on all Table 5 results, fine-grained pruning is preferable for tasks that are structurally sensitive, and global pruning is better when compression alone is the aim.
